I implemented `satisfies` and `maxSatisfying` in `src/semver.ts` as a dependency-free port of node-semver v7's range logic with default options. `bun test` passes (3 tests).

I also compared it against the real `semver@7.8.5`, which happened to be in the bun cache, using a throwaway script outside the repo (`/tmp/fz.ts`). It covered 63 ranges and 33 versions, including edge cases: `v`/`=` prefixes, `||` with an empty side, `<x`, leading zeros, build metadata, invalid ranges, and prereleases only being allowed on the same `major.minor.patch`. Both functions gave the same answer as the real package in every case.

I skipped the `loose` and `includePrerelease` options, since the task only asks for default behaviour. I didn't test very large version numbers or node-semver's protection against slow regexes on huge inputs, so very long range strings could match slowly.
